finding_key: docs/tasks/active/20260710-docs-list-updatedat-webhook-todo.md::the originating task's verification criterion for an e2e test of the webhook path is not met
evidence: The task file's Verification block (docs/tasks/active/20260710-docs-list-updatedat-webhook-todo.md, "## Verification": "e2e: signed webhook advances `updatedAt`; unsigned/bad-sig rejected") asserts e2e coverage, but the diff adds only three unit specs — yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts, yorkie-signature.guard.spec.ts, document.service.spec.ts — each constructing the class directly with a mocked DocumentService/PrismaService; no new file appears under packages/backend/test/, and the supplied directory listing of that folder at this commit (14 entries) contains no yorkie/webhook e2e spec. So nothing exercises the route through Nest's HTTP stack: the `bodyParser.json({ verify })` raw-body capture in packages/backend/src/main.ts (whose `req.url === '/internal/yorkie/events'` match is exactly the kind of wiring only an HTTP-level test catches), the guard registration in document.module.ts, and the monotonic `updateMany` SQL in touchUpdatedAt are all untested end to end. The Tasks section itself concedes "DB-backed e2e for the advance-only path deferred", which contradicts the Verification claim rather than satisfying it. Impact is limited to documentation accuracy plus a coverage gap on a security-relevant guard, not a user-visible defect.
